minutes.headline: Parks Commission rescinded its septic vote, then approved a Marshall Park septic and toilet plan 3-1; funding left unresolved.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a heated debate over Marshall Park: accepting Board of Health money for a septic system and toilet building, and whether to build before the engineering and funding exist. The commission rescinded the prior vote and passed a new motion, then tabled a funding-condition motion and agreed to seek a joint meeting with the Board of Health. It also covered the town beach season, the select board presentation, capital planning, the beach closing date, and recreation updates.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission rescinded its earlier vote on Board of Health money for a Marshall Park septic system, on a roll call with all four voting aye.
The commission then voted 3-1 to accept the Board of Health offer and plan, fund and build a Marshall Park septic system and toilet facility.
A motion barring construction until funding is secured for the whole project was set aside, and the audio does not record a vote on it.
The commission agreed to seek a joint in-person meeting with the Board of Health within about two months, and the chair will send dates.
The commission wants the town beach open through Labor Day if staffing allows, and members will bring 2024 capital requests to the next meeting on August 17.

why_it_matters: The Marshall Park vote commits the commission to a septic and toilet project whose engineering and full funding are not yet settled, so the Board of Health money may not cover the whole cost.

Prevailing wage rules and the town's up-front payment of grant costs can raise what public construction costs compared with a private install, so residents may later see requests for more town money, such as select board funds or a capital article.
watch_next: The joint meeting with the Board of Health, which the chair is to schedule within about two months.
The August 17 Parks Commission meeting, where members bring 2024 capital project requests.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the rescission vote, the 3-1 vote to accept the Board of Health offer, the Labor Day decision and the $20,000 capital-plan threshold. The main differences are a second 4-0 motion that only the official minutes record, a joint meeting that ours says is with the Board of Health and the official says is with the Select Board, and a next-meeting date of August 17 in ours against August 2 and 17 in the official minutes.
